title: Ring all-reduce, 4x4x4 torus (64 chips)
intro:
All-reduce gives every chip the sum of every chip's data. Training uses it after each step: every chip computes gradients on its own batch, and all of them need the total. Large all-reduces run in two halves. In the reduce-scatter half, chips trade pieces and add what they receive, until each chip owns the finished sum for one slice of the buffer. In the all-gather half, each chip sends its finished slice to everyone, so every chip ends with the whole sum. Each dot is one transfer.

On a torus the data is split into three shards, A, B and C, one per colour. Each shard reduces along X, then Y, then Z, starting in a different dimension, so all six links of every chip are busy at every step. That uses all the bandwidth, but it takes 18 steps one after another, and each step waits for the slowest link.
segments: Each ring of 4 chips passes pieces around in 3 steps, adding as it goes. Shards move along: A on X, B on Y, C on Z. After this phase each shard is summed over 4 chips and each chip keeps a quarter of what it held, so the dots shrink.

The reverse: finished slices are copied back around the rings (B on X, C on Y, A on Z), and each chip's share grows fourfold.
